new.brief: Creates a new event controller that will handle scroll events.
new.md: Creates a new event controller that will handle scroll events.

doc.md:
Handles scroll events.

It is capable of handling both discrete and continuous scroll
events from mice or touchpads, abstracting them both with the
[`EventControllerScroll::scroll`](xref:gtk:Gtk.EventControllerScroll#event:scroll) signal. Deltas in
the discrete case are multiples of 1.

In the case of continuous scroll events, `GtkEventControllerScroll`
encloses all [`EventControllerScroll::scroll`](xref:gtk:Gtk.EventControllerScroll#event:scroll) emissions
between two [`EventControllerScroll::scroll-begin`](xref:gtk:Gtk.EventControllerScroll#event:scroll-begin) and
[`EventControllerScroll::scroll-end`](xref:gtk:Gtk.EventControllerScroll#event:scroll-end) signals.

The behavior of the event controller can be modified by the flags
given at creation time, or modified at a later point through
[`EventControllerScroll.set_flags()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.EventControllerScroll#method:set_flags) (e.g. because the scrolling
conditions of the widget changed).

The controller can be set up to emit motion for either/both vertical
and horizontal scroll events through %GTK_EVENT_CONTROLLER_SCROLL_VERTICAL,
%GTK_EVENT_CONTROLLER_SCROLL_HORIZONTAL and %GTK_EVENT_CONTROLLER_SCROLL_BOTH_AXES.
If any axis is disabled, the respective [`EventControllerScroll::scroll`](xref:gtk:Gtk.EventControllerScroll#event:scroll)
delta will be 0. Vertical scroll events will be translated to horizontal
motion for the devices incapable of horizontal scrolling.

The event controller can also be forced to emit discrete events on all
devices through %GTK_EVENT_CONTROLLER_SCROLL_DISCRETE. This can be used
to implement discrete actions triggered through scroll events (e.g.
switching across combobox options).

The %GTK_EVENT_CONTROLLER_SCROLL_KINETIC flag toggles the emission of the
[`EventControllerScroll::decelerate`](xref:gtk:Gtk.EventControllerScroll#event:decelerate) signal, emitted at the end
of scrolling with two X/Y velocity arguments that are consistent with the
motion that was received.

get_flags.brief: Gets the flags conditioning the scroll controller behavior.
get_flags.md: Gets the flags conditioning the scroll controller behavior.

get_unit.brief: Gets the scroll unit of the last [`EventControllerScroll::scroll`](xref:gtk:Gtk.EventControllerScroll#event:scroll) signal received.
get_unit.md:
Gets the scroll unit of the last
[`EventControllerScroll::scroll`](xref:gtk:Gtk.EventControllerScroll#event:scroll) signal received.

Always returns %GDK_SCROLL_UNIT_WHEEL if the
%GTK_EVENT_CONTROLLER_SCROLL_DISCRETE flag is set.

set_flags.brief: Sets the flags conditioning scroll controller behavior.
set_flags.md: Sets the flags conditioning scroll controller behavior.

flags.brief: The flags affecting event controller behavior.
flags.md: The flags affecting event controller behavior.

decelerate.brief: Emitted after scroll is finished if the %GTK_EVENT_CONTROLLER_SCROLL_KINETIC flag is set.
decelerate.md:
Emitted after scroll is finished if the
%GTK_EVENT_CONTROLLER_SCROLL_KINETIC flag is set.

`vel_x` and `vel_y` express the initial velocity that was
imprinted by the scroll events. `vel_x` and `vel_y` are expressed in
pixels/ms.

scroll.brief: Signals that the widget should scroll by the amount specified by `dx` and `dy`.
scroll.md:
Signals that the widget should scroll by the
amount specified by `dx` and `dy`.

For the representation unit of the deltas, see
[`EventControllerScroll.get_unit()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.EventControllerScroll#method:get_unit).

scroll-begin.brief: Signals that a new scrolling operation has begun.
scroll-begin.md:
Signals that a new scrolling operation has begun.

It will only be emitted on devices capable of it.

scroll-end.brief: Signals that a scrolling operation has finished.
scroll-end.md:
Signals that a scrolling operation has finished.

It will only be emitted on devices capable of it.
